verifier_note: Checked all 49 warrant sources by direct retrieval (Rust Reference/Book/Nomicon/std docs on doc.rust-lang.org, 6 version-announcement blog posts, RFC 2451, PR rust-lang/rust#133372, lang-team issue #286, and 4 rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 docs.rs source files) and every engine_note claim against the live si-rpg-engine repo (solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, solver/Cargo.toml, solver/Cargo.lock, docs/dispatch-t2-restore.md) via gh api. I also ran all 77 of the lane's checks myself through scripts/compile_oracle.py against the real pinned rustc 1.98.1 with rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 / parry3d-f64 0.30.2 exactly as locked in Cargo.lock: 77/77 passed, reproducing rustc's exact wording verbatim ("is not dyn compatible", "missing required bound on `Item`" with no code, the literal `DVec3` name in the E0117 note for Rapier's Vector, "required for `Log` to implement `MaybeSync`", "is a \"sealed trait\"", "the struct `Cell<T>` is invariant..."). No source misattribution, no stale API, no check/prose mismatch, and no engine-fact error found in any of the 10 recipes. Systemic weakness: several softening "gotchas" clauses are asserted but not independently exercised by that recipe's own checks[] — recipe 1 claims associated consts and GATs make a trait dyn-incompatible with no check of its own (only recipe 2's checks demonstrate it), and recipe 9 claims a sealed trait still permits calling its public methods from outside without ever demonstrating that call. A reader who trusted only checks[] as ground truth would not catch a regression in these secondary claims.
